office_does: State Representatives write and vote on state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets; each district elects two to two-year terms.
race_blurb: Open seat: Republican Katy Cornell, a nonprofit leader and pastor endorsed by the outgoing incumbent, faces Democrat Renee Hernandez Greenfield, an educator and union faculty representative. They split on climate, taxes, housing regulation and reproductive policy.

candidates.summary: Nonprofit leader, pastor and Gig Harbor planning commissioner running as a 'common-sense Republican' on affordability, public safety and smaller government.
highlights: Would oppose the income tax and reverse ESSB 5814's sales tax on services [S3]
Would cut housing regulations, impact fees and red tape [S3][S7]
Would extend Clean Energy Transformation Act deadlines to 2040 [S6]
Supports court-mandated treatment for repeat offenders and stronger prosecution of property crime [S3][S5]

taxes.basis: Calls for 'smarter spending, not higher taxes', opposes the income tax and would reverse ESSB 5814.

spending.basis: Wants to reduce waste and bureaucracy and streamline government, without cutting core services.

housing.basis: Would reduce regulations, impact fees and mandates and streamline permitting to lower building costs.

safety.basis: Supports court-mandated treatment, stronger prosecution of repeat property crime, consequences for hard-drug possession and license plate readers.

climate.basis: Would extend CETA clean-energy deadlines to 2040 to limit utility costs.

experience.basis: First legislative run after service on the Gig Harbor Planning Commission; endorsers cite 'fresh energy'.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate, special educator and Tacoma Community College adjunct, running on schools, housing costs, climate and abortion rights.
highlights: Calls herself 'a steadfast champion of strong climate policies'; endorsed by Washington Conservation Action [S1][S2]
Pledges to keep Washington '100 percent pro-choice'; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates [S1][S2]
Would fight tax increases on working and middle-class families and cut wasteful state spending [S2]
Endorsed by the Washington State Labor Council and the Washington Education Association [S1]

spending.basis: Wants to cut wasteful state spending while saying schools do more with less and childcare subsidies are underfunded.

climate.basis: Champions clean energy, carbon reduction and polluter accountability; endorsed by Washington Conservation Action.

experience.basis: First-time candidate whose only elected role is a union faculty representative.

social.basis: Pledges a '100 percent pro-choice' Washington; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates.
